items.event_title: Houthi attacks disrupt Saudi energy facilities as Brent approaches $100
items.news_summary: Houthi missile and drone attacks hit southern Saudi cities and disrupted operations at energy facilities; 73 people were reported wounded. Brent rose to about $98 and U.S. crude to about $93.65 as the wider U.S.-Iran conflict intensified.
items.investor_materiality: A Saudi supply disruption layered onto an already tight geopolitical backdrop can move inflation expectations, Fed pricing, energy equities, airlines, transports and the broad U.S. equity multiple.
items.selection_reason: The strongest cross-asset catalyst in the window because it combines physical energy disruption, geopolitical escalation and immediate oil-price movement.
items.source_quality_note: Reuters reporting cites Saudi energy authorities and market prices; damage assessment is still evolving.

items.event_title: ASML works with major chipmakers to adapt High-NA EUV for larger data-center chips
items.news_summary: ASML plans to work with Intel, TSMC, Samsung and SK Hynix on larger masks that would let High-NA EUV tools manufacture larger data-center processors while improving productivity. Intel is already using High-NA in some production; Samsung and SK Hynix target DRAM use around 2028 and TSMC around 2030.
items.investor_materiality: The roadmap affects ASML tool demand and the manufacturing path for future AI accelerators, memory and foundry nodes used by Nvidia, Google and other hyperscalers.
items.selection_reason: A concrete next-generation lithography roadmap with direct read-through across the AI semiconductor capital-equipment chain.
items.source_quality_note: Reuters reporting on ASML's announced collaboration and chipmaker timelines.

items.selection_reason: A named customer, multi-year contract and new geography make this a concrete AI-capex catalyst rather than generic data-center commentary.
items.source_quality_note: Reuters reporting on the signed agreement; detailed economics were not disclosed in the report.

items.event_title: Mistral raises €3 billion at roughly $24 billion valuation
items.news_summary: French AI company Mistral raised €3 billion at about a €21 billion ($24 billion) valuation in Europe's largest private-tech equity round, with Samsung and an EU-backed fund among investors. Management expects about $1 billion ARR by year-end.
items.investor_materiality: The round provides a new valuation benchmark for frontier AI, supports European sovereign-AI spending and has competitive read-through for Microsoft, cloud providers and model platforms.
items.selection_reason: A very large fresh funding round with a concrete valuation and revenue benchmark in the global frontier-model race.
items.source_quality_note: Reuters reported the financing size, valuation, investors and management ARR target.

items.event_title: Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect as U.S. trade talks stall
items.news_summary: Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs on about $20 billion of U.S. goods at rates ranging from 15% to 50% after bilateral talks stalled, escalating the cross-border trade dispute.
items.investor_materiality: The tariffs can raise costs across autos, steel, furniture, apparel and electronics while increasing North American inflation and margin uncertainty.
items.selection_reason: A policy measure actually taking effect, rather than tariff rhetoric, with broad U.S.-equity and supply-chain consequences.

items.event_title: Yen reaches seven-month high as markets price a near-term BOJ hike
items.news_summary: The yen strengthened to 152.89 per dollar, its strongest in about seven months, as markets increased bets on a 25-basis-point BOJ hike to 1.25% at the September 17-18 meeting. The move is pressuring yen-funded carry trades.
items.investor_materiality: A rapid yen rally and carry-trade unwind can spill into global liquidity, U.S. tech positioning, Treasury flows and Japanese equities.
items.selection_reason: A large currency move tied to a near-term central-bank repricing creates a direct global risk-asset transmission channel.
items.source_quality_note: Reuters market reporting with live FX levels, policy probabilities and positioning context.

items.event_title: Longsys completes $903 million Hong Kong share sale amid AI-memory boom
items.news_summary: Chinese storage maker Longsys debuted in Hong Kong after raising about $903 million. First-half 2026 net profit rose to 10.7 billion yuan, more than 260 times the prior-year level, while revenue rose 136.3%, with AI-related demand cited as a driver.
items.investor_materiality: The numbers are a strong memory-cycle read-through for DRAM/NAND pricing, AI storage demand and U.S.-listed memory peers such as Micron and SanDisk.
items.selection_reason: A large fresh capital raise paired with extraordinary profit/revenue growth provides concrete evidence on the AI-memory cycle.
items.source_quality_note: Reuters reports IPO proceeds and company financial figures from the Hong Kong listing context.

items.news_summary: Bloomberg reported that Anthropic decided not to acquire AI startup Decart after due diligence; talks had contemplated a price of roughly $6 billion, though no deal had been finalized.
items.investor_materiality: The abandoned deal sheds light on frontier-AI acquisition discipline and potential competition for AI talent, model technology and cloud spending.
items.selection_reason: A multibillion-dollar strategic transaction being abandoned is a fresh, identifiable event in the private AI arms race.
references: Bloomberg News via Bloomberg Law, Sep. 8, 2026
items.source_quality_note: Bloomberg cites people familiar with the matter; both companies declined comment, so the deal value and diligence process remain reported rather than officially confirmed.
